title: Fence Painting & Staining in Hawthorne, FL
description: Fence painting and staining in Hawthorne, FL for wood privacy fences, pickets, and vinyl. Repairs, mildew cleaning, and stain or paint matched to the wood.
h1: Fence Painting and Staining in Hawthorne, FL
heroIntro: A fence takes more weather per square foot than anything else on the lot. We clean, repair, and coat it so it stops graying, splitting, and turning green at the base.

questions: Should I paint or stain my wood fence in Hawthorne?
Can a vinyl fence be painted?
Why does the bottom of my fence turn green and rot first?

body: Fence boards are thin, exposed on both faces, and set close to wet ground. In Hawthorne that means the bottom few inches stay damp through the rainy season, sprinkler heads soak the same pickets daily, and anything near the lakes grows mildew fast. The sunny face of the same fence bleaches gray and starts to check. Fence painting in Hawthorne, FL starts with a walk of the whole run to see which of those problems you have and where. The same crew lead who handles painting jobs throughout Hawthorne does that walk.
Sun-bleached fences are common across the county; our article on treating a sun-damaged wood fence in Alachua County covers how far gone is too far.

sections.h2: Paint or stain? A practical way to decide
bullets: Stain when the wood is in decent shape and you like the grain; it soaks in and will not peel
Solid stain when boards are mismatched from past repairs but you still want a wood texture
Paint when the fence is already painted, or you want a crisp color that matches the house trim
Avoid switching from paint back to stain unless the old film is fully stripped
body: Most wood privacy fences in town get a penetrating stain, because it works with the wood instead of forming a film that moisture can push off.

We clean mildew and dirt with a soft wash, let the wood dry, and check every post and rail. Loose pickets are re-fastened, broken ones replaced, and rails that have pulled away are reset before anything is coated. Sprayed stain is back-brushed so it works into the grain and the end cuts. On painted fences, loose paint is scraped and bare spots primed first.
Vinyl fences can be painted with the right product system once they are thoroughly cleaned, which is a good option when the color has faded or chalked.

sections.h2: Getting more years out of the base of the fence
body: The ground line is where most Hawthorne fences give out. A few simple changes help the new finish last: trim grass and shrubs back so air moves along the base, re-aim sprinkler heads that hit the same pickets every morning, and keep mulch from piling against the boards. During prep we pay extra attention to the bottom edge and the end grain of each picket, working stain into the cut ends where water wicks up fastest.

sections.h2: Coordinating with the house and deck
body: If the house is being repainted, we usually do the fence afterward so overspray and drips land on unfinished boards. Fences tied into a deck can be stained in the same visit as the deck restoration, and a pre-wash can be scheduled with our Hawthorne soft-wash service. For product and stain details, see our Florida deck and fence staining page.

faqs.q: How long does fence staining take in Hawthorne?
faqs.a: Most residential fences are cleaned one day and stained once the wood has dried. The exact schedule depends on length, height, and repairs, and it is written on the estimate.

faqs.q: Do you stain both sides of the fence?
faqs.a: We can. Both faces are listed separately on the estimate, since the neighbor-facing side sometimes needs permission or a different schedule.

faqs.q: Can you replace broken pickets before staining?
faqs.a: Yes. Loose pickets are re-fastened and damaged ones replaced during prep so the finished fence reads as one surface.
